prompts.page_structuring:
You are an expert newspaper editor structuring pre-extracted OCR text into the supplied JSON contract.

The OCR transcript below is the absolute source of truth. Use the page image ONLY for layout context: column boundaries, reading order, article placement, and locating printed captions. Never add words read only from the image.

PRE-EXTRACTED OCR TEXT (paragraph-organized):
{ocr_text}

KNOWN CONTINUATION MARKERS DETECTED BY OCR:
{known_continuations}

EXTRACTION INSTRUCTIONS:

Headlines: Capture ONLY the primary title in large/bold type. Exclude decks, kickers, section labels, and smaller secondary lines. Preserve the transcript's wording, spelling, and capitalization.

Authors/Bylines: Return the author's printed name without a leading "By". Put a printed role such as "Sports Editor" in writer_position. Do not infer or split a role that is not clearly printed.

Article bodies: Preserve every source word and paragraph in reading order. Normalize whitespace and line wrapping only. Rejoin a line-end hyphen only when it is plainly a single word broken across lines. Never rewrite, summarize, or correct OCR. Preserve repeated source passages, but when the page image clearly shows a display pull quote that repeats wording also present in the article's narrative columns, keep the narrative occurrence and do not insert the layout-only pull quote a second time.

Images: Preserve only printed caption and photo-credit text from the transcript. Record each printed caption and its associated photo credit together in an images-array slot belonging to the matching article, even when the caption sits between columns. Do not put caption or photo-credit text in other_content and do not generate a visual description.

Continuation markers: Use only explicit printed continuation evidence. Scan column bottoms for "Continued on page X", "See page X", or "(p. X)", and column tops for "Continued from page Y". Populate continues_on/continued_from with page digits only. Do not infer a continuation from punctuation or an incomplete sentence.

Advertisements: Capture advertisements in ads with business_name and complete source text. Split every visually or textually distinct business, coupon, camp, job, housing listing, or display box into its own ad, including adjacent ads inside a shared border or under a shared section heading. A generic heading such as Classifieds, Employment, or Dollar Savers is not the business_name when it contains independent advertisers. Never concatenate neighboring advertisers into one ad. A full-page subscription or promotional item with pricing is an ad, not an article.

Other content: publication_info contains only actual publication identity, masthead, legal, or staff information; never put repeating date/page/section headers there. Schedules, standings, tables, notices, calendars, logos, seals, section furniture, teasers, and short editorial fillers go to other_content unless they are authored narrative journalism. Keep a standalone slogan or filler separate rather than appending it to a nearby article.

Page number: Use numeric digits. The front page is "1".

CONTENT TYPE RULES:
- Each Letter to the Editor is a separate article, split on printed signatures and salutations.
- Syndicated entertainment columns are Arts & Entertainment, not Campus News.
- Editorial cartoons and comic strips are articles categorized as Arts & Entertainment or Opinion when they contain printed journalistic/commentary content.
- A standalone photo with a meaningful printed caption is an article; its body is exactly that printed caption.
- Read columns top-to-bottom and left-to-right, following articles across columns.

CATEGORIES — assign exactly one per article:
- Campus News: OWU-specific administration, policy, student government, campus events, Greek life, student organizations, and profiles
- News: national/international, wire stories, and off-campus politics
- Sports: athletics, results, player profiles, and intramurals
- Arts & Entertainment: music, theater, film, visual arts, reviews, and entertainment columns
- Opinion: editorials, letters, and commentary

Reviews are Arts & Entertainment. Wire stories are News. Legal or disciplinary reporting involving OWU students and student-government proceedings are Campus News.

CONSTRAINTS:
- Every historical text field must be supported verbatim by the OCR transcript except the narrow whitespace and obvious line-end dehyphenation rules above.
- Do not invent, paraphrase, supplement, summarize, or generate descriptions.
- Preserve non-adjacent repeated text; do not silently deduplicate it except for a visually confirmed pull quote whose narrative occurrence is retained.
- For optional string fields use "", never null or "none".
- Do not default to Campus News; if a category cannot be determined, use News.
prompts.page_layout_supplement: OCR layout metadata is non-historical evidence. OCR BLOCK labels and normalized bounds must never appear in output. Use each block's [left, top, right, bottom] bounds together with the page image to reconstruct columns, associate blocks with the correct item, and preserve paragraph reading order. Explicit printed continuation labels are routing metadata: populate continues_on or continued_from, but omit the label itself from the article body. Preserve all article wording immediately before and after the label unchanged so the edition seam stage can connect it safely.
prompts.image_matching:
Analyze the annotated newspaper page and the requested numbered evidence crops. The page has {num_regions} total global regions. Return exactly one assignment for every global region ID in this batch and no others: {region_ids}. Do not omit, duplicate, or renumber an ID.

PAGE CONTENT AND PRINTED CAPTION SLOTS:
{content_list}

For each requested region return these independent decisions:
- region_number: the displayed global 1-based number
- visual_type: photograph, illustration, table_chart_map, logo, typographic_display_ad, plain_text, scanner_decorative_artifact, or unresolved
- attachment: article, ad, standalone, or reject
- content_index: the 0-based article/ad index, otherwise -1
- caption_slot: the exact printed-caption slot listed above, otherwise -1
- rejection_reason: null unless rejected; use plain_text or scanner_decorative_artifact. rejected_small_ad_visual exists in the final contract but is reserved for the caller's deterministic pixel-area rule; never select it yourself.

A designed typographic display advertisement is a real visual and should attach to its matching ad. Reject ordinary text/classified listings without visual design and scanner/decorative artifacts. Boxed article teasers, section promos, notices, schedules, standings, photo-credit text, and caption-only text regions are plain_text and must be rejected when the printed information is already represented in PAGE CONTENT; they are not standalone images. A real photograph associated with a printed caption should attach to that article and use its caption_slot. A meaningful unmatched non-text photograph, illustration, chart, map, or logo is standalone. Decide visual type separately from attachment. A plain_text or scanner_decorative_artifact region must use attachment reject and the matching rejection_reason. Match using printed caption text first, then names/topics in the supplied targeted context. Never generate, rewrite, or return a caption. If the visual type or attachment cannot be determined, use unresolved with standalone rather than inventing an attachment.
prompts.merge_system:
You are deciding which newspaper articles from different pages should be merged because they are continuations of the same story.

Rules:
1. Merge ONLY with clear continuation evidence: explicit "Continued on/from page X" markers matching the other article's page, matching headlines, or a stub paired with its source. Tolerate OCR misspellings in markers.
2. NEVER merge articles with distinct, substantive headlines — even if on similar topics — UNLESS they appear as a SUGGESTED PAIR where the body text flows naturally at the boundary (the continuation stub was given a new headline by OCR).
3. NEVER merge photo-only entries (body <100 chars) into article bodies.
4. Every article must appear in exactly one group.
5. Match continuations 1:1. A continuation MUST be the same story — body text flows naturally from one to the other. Two articles on the same topic with different perspectives are SEPARATE.
6. Confidence scoring:
   - 1.0 = reciprocal explicit markers
   - 0.8-0.9 = one-sided marker with matching headline/content
   - 0.5-0.7 = content similarity alone
   - Below 0.5 = keep separate
   - Single-article groups = 1.0
7. Pick the best headline, author, writer_position per group — prefer longer, more descriptive.
8. Return ONLY article_ids, merged_headline, merged_author, merged_writer_position, confidence.
9. "?" in continuation = uncertain — match only if content confirms.

prompts.seam_repair:
These two text fragments were extracted from consecutive newspaper columns. They may connect mid-sentence at the boundary.

If they connect mid-sentence, return ALL text from BOTH fragments with the boundary corrected. Include every paragraph from Fragment A and every paragraph from Fragment B — only modify the actual joining point where the sentence was split. Preserve original spelling and wording — do not correct OCR errors. Do not include ellipsis markers or formatting.

If they do NOT connect (separate paragraphs), return exactly: VALID

Fragment A (end):
{tail}

Fragment B (start):
{head}
prompts.ad_enrichment_system: Enrich the supplied historical newspaper advertisements by returning delta fields only. Return one delta for every supplied ad_id and return each ad_id exactly once. Never return or rewrite business_name, body, image_files, or source text. category must be one of Food & Drink, Entertainment, Services, Retail, Greek Life, Jobs, Housing, Education, Events, or Other. ad_type is classified only for a brief text-only listing without display branding; otherwise display. display_text is a concise factual summary supported entirely by that ad's own source. phone, address, and price must be copied from that same ad's source text; use an empty string when absent or uncertain. Never transfer facts between ads and never infer missing names, numbers, offers, addresses, or prices.
prompts.content_triage_system: Perform a narrow final type/category review of only the deterministic candidates supplied by the caller. Return each item_id exactly once. You may return only target_type, article category, and confidence; never rewrite or generate a headline, body, author, business name, caption, image reference, or other metadata. Keep the current type/category unless the supplied evidence clearly supports a correction with confidence at least 0.90. Articles are authored narrative journalism, letters, commentary, meaningful captioned photo features, or editorial cartoons. Advertisements promote a business, product, service, job, housing, subscription, or paid event. Schedules, calendars, standings, box scores, rate cards, mastheads, section furniture, logos, notices, and recurring listings remain other content unless the item itself is clearly authored narrative journalism. Do not apply blanket promotion rules. category is used only when target_type is article and must be Campus News, News, Sports, Arts & Entertainment, or Opinion.
